Simulated datasets from a model

Source: R/ilm_sim.R, R/zzz-iml-aliases.R
ilm_sim.Rd

Whole datasets drawn from a fitted model or an ilm_scaffold(): each row's own columns, with a simulated response in place of the observed one. A shortcut for ilm_simulate(), whose matrix of responses would otherwise have to be bound back to the rows by hand.

Usage

ilm_sim(object, nsim = 1L, seed = NULL, n = NULL, effect = NULL, term = NULL)

Arguments

object

A fitted ilm_model(), or an ilm_scaffold().

nsim

Integer. Number of datasets.

seed

Integer. Random seed, for reproducibility. With NULL the draws come from the current random stream, as ilm_simulate()'s do.

n

The number of rows in each simulated study, as in ilm_power(); NULL keeps the rows the model was fitted to.

effect

The tested coefficient's value on the link scale, or a multiple of a term's coefficients, as in ilm_power(); NULL keeps the fitted values.

term

The coefficient or term effect sets, named as in ilm_power().

Value

A data frame when nsim = 1, and otherwise a list of nsim data frames.

The rows

The columns are the ones the model reads: the response, the variables its terms are built from, its grouping factors and weights, and the variables of an offset, a dispersion model and a zero part. The rows are the ones it was fitted to, so a row it dropped for a missing value is not there. For a scaffold they are its design grid.

With neither n nor effect, the responses are ilm_simulate()'s, draw for draw with the same seed. The rows and their group labels are the fitted ones, and each dataset draws new random effects for those groups, so it is a new sample of groups under the old labels.

A study of another size or effect

n draws a study of about that many rows, as ilm_power() draws one. A fitted model's rows are resampled, whole clusters at a time when it has a grouping factor, and a scaffold's design is laid out again at that size. A cluster drawn twice is two clusters: the unit is renumbered by the copy drawn, 1, 2, and so on, a grouping factor nested in it is prefixed with its copy ("2.b"), and one crossed with it, such as items every participant sees, keeps its labels. A row with a frequency weight is drawn as that many rows, each with weight 1.

effect draws the data with one coefficient, or one term, changed, as in ilm_power(): for a single coefficient, its value on the link scale; for a term of several coefficients, a multiple of them, so effect = 0.5 halves it. term names it, and defaults to the first coefficient that is not an intercept.

The response

The simulated response goes in the response's own column, of the same type: a factor stays a factor with the same levels, a logical stays logical, and a whole-number count stays integer. The response has to be a column the formula names, not a calculation on one such as log(y); for that, ilm_simulate() returns the response on the scale the model fits.

A censored response is censored as ilm_simulate() censors it, and a column beside it says what ilm_model()'s censor needs to fit it again:

  • a survival time gets .event, 1 where the event was drawn and 0 where the time was cut at the subject's censoring time, as ilm_surv() takes it: ilm_surv(d$time, d$.event);

  • codes given to ilm_censor() as status are held fixed by the draw, and come back as .censored: ilm_censor(d$y, status = d$.censored);

  • a floor or ceiling needs no column, because the drawn values are held at it and ilm_censor() finds them again: ilm_censor(d$y, lower = 0).

See also

ilm_simulate() for the responses alone, ilm_power() to count detections over many simulated studies, ilm_refit() to refit the same model, and illumex::ilm_example_data() for example data of a fixed design.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(id = factor(rep(1:12, each = 6)), x = rnorm(72))
d$y <- 1 + 0.5 * d$x + rnorm(12)[d$id] + rnorm(72)
fit <- ilm_model(y ~ x + (1 | id), data = d, family = "gaussian",
                 verbose = FALSE)
head(ilm_sim(fit, seed = 2))
#>            y          x id
#> 1 -0.7448145 -0.6264538  1
#> 2 -0.9491267  0.1836433  1
#> 3  0.9619524 -0.8356286  1
#> 4 -1.4237852  1.5952808  1
#> 5  0.6902534  0.3295078  1
#> 6 -0.4705379 -0.8204684  1

## rehearse the analysis on a study of 120 rows, with half the slope
d2 <- ilm_sim(fit, n = 120, effect = 0.25, term = "x", seed = 3)
coef(ilm_model(y ~ x + (1 | id), data = d2, family = "gaussian",
               verbose = FALSE))
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   0.5277337   0.2235750 

## from a scaffold: three draws of a planned two-arm trial
s <- ilm_scaffold(y ~ arm, design = list(arm = c("control", "treatment")),
                  n_unit = 60, cells = c(control = 12, treatment = 14.5),
                  sd = 4, verbose = FALSE)
sims <- ilm_sim(s, nsim = 3, seed = 4)
sapply(sims, function(d) diff(tapply(d$y, d$arm, mean)))
#> treatment treatment treatment 
#>  1.330933  2.165573  1.838666
